units.tr: Piously and truly Augustine: faith, he says, is the foundation of all good things. Faith is the beginning of human salvation. Without it no one can come to be counted among the sons of God, because without it no one obtains the grace of justification in this world, nor can he attain eternal life in the future. Faith is, moreover (as the same Augustine says), to believe in him who justifies the ungodly; to believe in the Mediator, without whom no one is reconciled to God; to believe in the Saviour, who came to seek and to save what was lost, and so on.

units.la: Certe:sine hac fide impossibile est placere Deo. quin sine ea quae fiunt, in peccata conuertuntur omnia: Per hanc fidem Dominus & Saluator nostrer potestatem dedit filios Dei fieri, omnibus, qui credunt in nomen eius. Fides nobis imputatur ad iustitiam. Fide viuimus. Fide stamus. Fide purificantur corda nostra. Filij Dei sumus ac manemus per fidem, per fidem habitat Christus in cordibus nostris. Fide nemo perit, sed habet vitam aeternam. Fides in Christum est victoria nostra, qua vincimus satanam, mundum, adeoque propriam nostram carnem. Fidei denique finis est salus animarum. In hac vsitate nostra comparemus coram Deo, huius adiutorio clamamus: Abba Pater! His oculus est, qui intuitur Christum. Haec est auris, quae audit Christum. Hęc salutifica dextera est, quae apprehendit Christum ad dextram Patris in caelis sedentem, eumque tenet. Hoc pede, currimus ad Christum. Huius complexu, ipsam q. aeternitatem concludimus. Fons viuus perennis aquae fides est, cuius aqua salliunt in vitam vsque aeternam. Arbor optima est, quae non nisi optimus aedere fructus poterit. Opus autem est & donum Dei, quod mediante sacro sancto ministerio Verbi in cordibus incendit Deus per Spiritum suum sanctum: Quare haec pretiosissima vnio non nisi in agro Euangelico foditur, effoditur. Oleo sacramentorum nutritur. Precum subsidio firmatur. Per tribulationes & calamitates exercetur. Per spem & charitatem manifestatur: per intercessionem Christi conseruatur in vita, tentationibus, & morte. Tria igitur confidero, in quibus tota spes mea confisit, charitatem adoptionis, veritatem promissionis, potestatem redditionis. SCIO cui credidi, quia in charitate nimia adoptauit me, quia verax in promissione, quia potens in exhibitione. Hic est funiculus triplex, qui difficulter rumpitur. Haec est fiducia, qua Abraham immolaturus, qua placuit Abel, qua arcam aedificauit Noe, qua luctatus Iacob, (vt emblema nostrum liquido demonstrat) qua eminuit Ioseph, qua opprobria tulit Moses, qua sancti vicerunt regna, qua denique saluati sunt omnes sancti, quotquot iam inde a condito orbe, adhuc, & vsque in aeternum beatitudinem obtinuerunt, obtinent, obtinebunt aeternam.
units.tr: Certainly, without this faith it is impossible to please God; indeed, without it everything that is done is turned into sin. Through this faith our Lord and Saviour gave power to become sons of God to all who believe in his name. Faith is imputed to us for righteousness. We live by faith. We stand by faith. Our hearts are purified by faith. We are and remain sons of God through faith; Christ dwells in our hearts through faith. No one perishes by faith, but has eternal life. Faith in Christ is our victory, by which we overcome Satan, the world, and even our own flesh. Finally, the end of faith is the salvation of souls. By this faith we present ourselves before God; by its help we cry, Abba, Father! Its eye is what looks upon Christ; its ear is what hears Christ; its saving right hand is what grasps Christ, seated at the right hand of the Father in heaven, and holds him fast. With this foot we run to Christ; in his embrace we even shut up eternity itself. Faith is the living spring of perennial water, whose waters leap up into eternal life. It is an excellent tree, which can bear only excellent fruit. Yet it is also the work and gift of God, which God kindles in the hearts of believers through his Holy Spirit, through the sacred ministry of the Word. Therefore this most precious union is dug up and dug out only in the Gospel field. It is nourished by the oil of the sacraments, strengthened by the help of prayers, exercised through tribulations and calamities, made manifest through hope and charity, and preserved in life, in temptations and in death through the intercession of Christ. I therefore consider three things in which my whole hope rests: the love of adoption, the truth of the promise, and the power of performance. I know whom I have believed, because in great love he has adopted me, because he is true in his promise, and because he is powerful in his performance. This is the threefold cord that is hard to break. This is the confidence by which Abraham was ready to sacrifice, by which Abel pleased God, by which Noah built the ark, by which Jacob wrestled (as our emblem clearly shows), by which Joseph shone forth, by which Moses bore reproaches, by which the saints conquered kingdoms; and finally, by which all the saints have been saved, as many as from the foundation of the world have obtained, do obtain, and will obtain eternal blessedness, both now and forever.

units.la: O thesauris omnibus opulentior fides, o virtutibus corporalibus omnibus fides fortior!
units.tr: O faith, richer than all treasures! O faith, stronger than all bodily virtues!
THE NATURE OF CHARITY

units.la: Sustinet incursum cataclysm saxea moles, Imprimis ferro conglomerata graui:
units.tr: The rocky mass withstands the onslaught of the cataclysm, bound fast above all with heavy iron:

units.la: Sic mens diuini bene conglomerata fauore Flaminis, aduersum stat Phlegetontis aquas.
units.tr: So the mind, firmly bound by the favour of the divine Spirit, stands against the waters of Phlegethon.

units.la: Sim charitate potest quidem fides esse, sed non & prodesse, non Afrorum tantū sed totius quoq; Christiani Orbis Episcoporum ocellus August. infit. Propterquod & Apostolus Paulus, in Christo (inquit) Iesu neq; circumcisio aliquid valet, neq; præputium aliquid valet, sed fides quæ per dilectionem operatur. Hæc est ea dilectio, quæ fidei soboles & æmula hic saxea mole nixa confidet, dextra charam sobolem, sinistra librum cum cruce tenet, iuugitq; omnia Patientia Hierogly phicus agnus, inumbrante cælesti & mitissima-diuina Columba Spiritu S. Id vero significare vult nostrum, dilectionem fide vera niti tanquam rupe, eamq;, vt sit vera, e fide saluifica manare oportere, à qua formetur, quæque per hanc (aiente Apostolo) sit efficax: est vera charitas quæ ad κατὰ τὸν θεὸν diuini canonis exigitur atq; exercetur: Tincta in cruce & sanguine Christi, per quem omnia coġitata, dicta, & facta nostra accepta redduntur. Piam sane ac lepidam Pictũram! Ostende enim mihi fidem ex operibus charitatis & sufficiet mihi; aut mortua fides & simulacrum fidei erit, aut operum monilibus redimita ouabit, Operum autē, inquam, DILECTIONIS. Dilectio fortu est, vt mors, durus vt sepulcrum zelus; Pruna eius pruna sunt, ignūq; flamma diuina. Aqua multa non possunt extinguere dilectionem, nec flamina inundabunt eam: Si daret quis totam substantiam domus suæ pro hoc amore, plane contemneretur. Si linguis hominum loquar & Angelorum, charitatem autem non habeam, factus sum as resonans, aut cymbalum tinniens. Etsi habeam Prophetiam, & nouerim mysteria omnia, omnemq; scientiam, & si habeam totam fidem, adeo vt montes transferam, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil sum. Et si infumam alendis egenis omnes facultates meas, & si tradam corpus meum vt comburar, charitatem autem non habeam, nihil iuuor. Hæc est caput & apex præcepti illius noui Dn. Saluatoris. Hac discipuli eius cluemus. Hac legem eius implemus. Hæc moderatrix fit omnium consultationum, actionum, passionumq; simul nostrarum. Hæc patiens est: comis est: non inuidet: non est insolens: non inflatur: Nihil vt indecorum fastidit: non quærit quæ sua sunt, non irritatur: non cogitat malum: non gaudet de iniustitia: gaudet autem de iustitia: omnia suffert: omnia sperat: omnia sustinet. ab hac vtranq; qp aiunt, faciamus paginam. Ab hac Dn. Saluator Iudicium suum olim auspicabitur, consummabit, exequetur. Hæc maxima est, æterna durans. Vide ergo quam multa & quam magna desint, nihilq; prosint, si hac vna desuerit Charitas causa est & mater omnium virtutum, quæ si desit, s ustra habentur cetera, si adsit, habentur omnia. Omnia fiunt facilia charitate. Totam magnitudinem diuinorum eloquiorum & latitudinem secura possidet charitas. Si ergo non vacat omnes paginas sanctas perscrutari, omnia inuoluta sermonum euoluere, omnia scriptura rum secreta penetrare, tene charitatem, ibi pendent omnia, ita tenebis quod ibi didicisti, tenebis etiam quod nondum didicisti.
units.tr: Faith can indeed exist without charity, but it cannot profit, says Augustine, the eye not only of the bishops of Africa but of the whole Christian world. For this reason the Apostle Paul also says: In Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith which works through love. This is that love which, leaning on the rocky mass, here takes its stand as the offspring and rival of faith. With its right hand it holds a dear child, with its left a book with a cross, and the Patient Hieroglyphic Lamb yokes all things together, while the heavenly and most gentle divine Dove, the Holy Spirit, overshadows them. This is what our emblem wishes to signify: that love must rest on true faith as on a rock, and that, to be true, it must flow from saving faith, by which it is formed, and which through it (as the Apostle says) is made effective. This is the true charity that is required and practised according to the divine canon, κατὰ τὸν θεὸν, dyed in the cross and blood of Christ, through whom all our thoughts, words and deeds are received and made acceptable. A pious and charming picture indeed! For show me your faith from your works of charity, and it will be enough for me; otherwise faith is dead and only a semblance of faith, or it will exult, adorned with the necklaces of works, of works, I say, OF LOVE. Love is strong as death, zeal hard as the grave; its coals are coals of fire, a divine flame. Many waters cannot quench love, nor will floods drown it. If a man were to give all the substance of his house for this love, he would be utterly despised. If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not charity, I have become sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal. And though I have prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and though I have all faith so that I can move mountains, but have not charity, I am nothing. And though I spend all my goods feeding the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, but have not charity, it profits me nothing. This is the head and crown of that new precept of our Lord and Saviour. By this his disciples are known. By this we fulfil his law. This is the guide of all our deliberations, actions and sufferings alike. It is patient; it is kind; it does not envy; it is not puffed up; it is not arrogant; it disdains nothing unbecoming; it does not seek its own; it is not provoked; it thinks no evil; it does not rejoice in iniquity but rejoices in the truth; it bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things. From this, as they say, let us make both sides of the page. From this the Lord Saviour will one day begin, complete and execute his judgment. This is the greatest, and it endures for ever. See, then, how many and how great things are lacking, and profit nothing, if this one thing, charity, is missing. Charity is the cause and mother of all the virtues: if it is absent, the rest are counted as nothing; if it is present, all things are counted. All things become easy through charity. Charity securely possesses the whole greatness and breadth of the divine oracles. If, therefore, you have no leisure to search through all the holy pages, to unfold all the involved sayings, and to penetrate all the secrets of the Scriptures, hold fast to charity: all things hang upon it. Thus you will hold what you have learned there, and you will also hold what you have not yet learned.
Ioan. 3.
HOPE DOES NOT DISAPPOINT:

units.la: Charitatem sequitur spes, illa fidem, haec illam: Est autem spes divinitus infusa virtus, qua promissionibus divinis in Christo de futuris beneficiis alacriter inhaerēmus.
units.tr: Hope follows charity, as charity follows faith, and faith hope: Hope is a virtue divinely infused, by which we cleave cheerfully to the divine promises in Christ concerning future benefits.

units.la: Breuis illa quidem sed admodum luculenta spei descriptio.
units.tr: A brief but very clear description of hope.

units.la: Causa efficiens SPEI est Spiritus S. sicut dicitur: Benedictus es, & Deus Pater Dn. nostri Iesu Christi, qui ex multa sua misericordia regenuit nos in SPEM vivam. Fructus Spiritus sub vocabulo ἐλπίς.
units.tr: The efficient cause of HOPE is the Holy Spirit, as it is said: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy has begotten us again to a living HOPE. It is the fruit of the Spirit under the name ἐλπίς.
The subject of HOPE is the heart.

units.la: Obiectum: Christus qui rupes nostra in Christo, qui Petra & fundamentum.
units.tr: The object: Christ, who is our rock in Christ, who is the Rock and foundation.

units.la: Causa instrumentalis est verbum Dei in primisq; promissio gratia.
units.tr: The instrumental cause is the Word of God, and above all the promise of grace.
The form: patient expectation of future good things.

units.la: Materia: Futura bona cum corporis, tum inprimis animae, quae non videntur sed sperantur. Spes enim non est visibilium, sed invisibilium. Spes si cernatur non est spes: quod autem quis cernit, cur sperat? Si vero, quod non videmus, speramus, per patientiam expectamus.
units.tr: The matter: future goods, both of the body and above all of the soul, which are not seen but hoped for. For hope is not of things seen, but of things unseen. If hope is seen, it is not hope; for why does a man hope for what he sees? But if we hope for what we do not see, we wait for it with patience.

units.la: Praeclare certe & omnino Christiane de spe Augustinus; Audite, inquit; & discite & tenete, quae sit spes Christianorum. Quare sumus Christiani? Non enim ad hoc sumus Christiani, ut terrenam nobis felicitatem petamus, quam plerumque habent & latrones & scelerati. Ad aliam felicitatem nos sumus Christiani, quam tunc accipiemus, cum vita ipsius secul: tota transierit. Ergo promittitur nobis & carnis resurrectio, &c.
units.tr: Augustine speaks most clearly and altogether in a Christian way about hope: Listen, he says, and learn and hold fast what the hope of Christians is. Why are we Christians? For we are not Christians in order to seek earthly happiness, which robbers and wicked men very often also have. We are Christians for another happiness, which we shall receive when the life of this world has wholly passed away. Therefore the resurrection of the flesh, etc., is promised to us.

units.la: Et idem alibi: Tribulatio nostra in praesenti seculo, spes vero nostra de futuro seculo: & nisi in tribulatione praesentis seculi, consoletur nos spes futuri seculi, perimus. Gaudium ergo nostrum, fratres, nondum est in re, sed in spe. SPES autem nostra tam certa est, quam si res iam perfecta fuit. Modo enim credimus, tum videbimus. Cum credimus spes est in isto seculo: cum videbimus res erit in futuro seculo. Haec Augustinus.
units.tr: And elsewhere the same: Our tribulation is in the present age, but our hope is of the age to come; and unless the hope of the age to come comforts us amid the tribulation of the present age, we perish. Therefore our joy, brethren, is not yet in possession but in hope. Our HOPE, however, is as certain as if the thing were already accomplished. For now we believe, then we shall see. When we believe, there is hope in this age; when we see, there will be the thing itself in the age to come. Thus Augustine.

units.la: Optume autem & appositissime anchora assimilatur ab Apostolo:
units.tr: Most fittingly and aptly the Apostle compares hope to an anchor.

units.la: Vita enim nostra est instar navigationis, nauigium cor est. Ancora spes: non tutius eiicitur, quam in rupe, rupes autem est Christus, nec maius quid priusve in ore habent navigantes quam patriam? patriam! cum praeda: & nostra onerosa oneris? in caelis est, unde expectamus Christum. Non igitur haereat anchora nostra in arena temporalium, sed in saxo Christo. Ea spes non confundit, non nutat, non deficit, durat usque in finem. Abscondita quidem anchora & spes seu vita nostra cum Christo in Deo, scimus autem, quod, quando vita illa nostra Christus patefactus fuerit, tum & nos apparituros in gloria. Ecce igitur, agricola expectat pretiosum fructum terrae, patienter ferens donec accipiat temporaneum & serotinum. Quanto magis nos sperare convenit & expectare! Beatus autem is est, qui hanc spem habet, fovetque. A similitudine illum viro prudenti, qui aedificavit domum suam (proiecerit anchora spei suae) super petram. Tunc descendit pluvia & venerunt flumina, & flaverunt venti, & inciderunt domui (naufragio) illi, & non cecidit, fundata enim fuerat super petram.
units.tr: For our life is like a voyage, and the ship is the heart. The anchor is hope: it is cast out no more securely than upon a rock, and the rock is Christ. Nor do sailors have anything greater or dearer on their lips than the homeland? The homeland! with its booty; and ours, burdened with a burden? It is in the heavens, whence we await Christ. Let our anchor not cling in the sand of temporal things, but in the rock, Christ. This hope does not disappoint; it does not waver or fail; it endures to the end. Hidden, indeed, is our anchor, and our hope or life is with Christ in God; but we know that when that life of ours, Christ, is made manifest, then we too shall appear in glory. Behold, then, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, bearing patiently until he receives the early and the late rain. How much more ought we to hope and to wait! Blessed, however, is he who has and cherishes this hope. Compare the wise man who built his house (who cast the anchor of his hope) upon a rock. Then the rain descended and the floods came, and the winds blew and beat upon that house (in shipwreck), and it did not fall, for it had been founded upon the rock.
Although
Faith Shines Through Hardships

units.la: [engraving: emblem, not transcribed as text] Per varios casus, per mille pericula rerum Mirificas sanctos, optime Christe, tuos: Turbida iucundum spero post nubila Phæbum, Dum præeat Verbum lampada opemq; tuum.
units.tr: Through many trials and a thousand dangers of the world, I wonder at your wonders, good Christ, and your saints. Though the stormy clouds hide the sun, I hope it will shine on me again, while your Word goes before me as a lamp and your help goes with me.

units.la: Cor quod hic vides,fidei signum est: facula autem ex corde figuram charitatem: Inter haec media fax, verbi, est: Alae fidei naturam depingunt. Nititur autem cor duabus dextris complicatis mutuo quae veritatem promissionis subinnuunt,& gemina crux, candida altera, altera nigra: crucis Christi, naturaeq; signis: a quibus liber dependet legis indicium: & cornu copiae, abundantiae σημεῖον.
units.tr: The heart you see here is a sign of faith, and the torch coming out of the heart represents love. Between them is a middle torch, of the Word. The wings depict the nature of faith. The heart rests on two right hands clasped together, which hint at the truth of the promise, and on a double cross, one white, the other black, which are signs of the cross of Christ and of nature. From these hangs a book, the sign of the law, and a horn of plenty, a sign of abundance [σημεῖον].

units.la: Fides est suavis genitrix, dulcisq; nutricula dilectionis, per quam, ut Apostolus loquitur, est efficax: Non est vera sed falsa, non recta sed fucata, non viva sed mortua fides, quae flammas charitatis non eiaculatur, longeque & late diffundit. Fides quatenus in corde latet, soli Deo visibilis est: hominib. autem videtur in operibus charitatis, quare est ipse Salvator in illa iudicii die non nisi per opera misericordiae ἐνεργούμενην fidem commendabit, inque lucem producet.
units.tr: Faith is the sweet mother and the gentle nurse of love, through which, as the Apostle says, it is effective. Faith that does not throw out the flames of love and spread them far and wide is not true but false, not right but feigned, not living but dead. Faith lies hidden in the heart and is visible to God alone; but it is seen by men in the works of love. Therefore, on the day of judgment, the Saviour himself will commend faith only through works of mercy, and bring it into the light, faith working through love [ἐνεργούμενην].

units.la: Fides itidem non haeret in terrenis, sed alis subvolat in caelum, ad thronum maiestatis divinae: Aquilae sunt fideles, non gracculi: conuersatio fidelium in caelis est, unde exspectant Christum Salvatorem. Quarunt quae supra sunt, ibi Christus est sedens ad dextram Dei. Ibi hic Thesaurum esse suum norunt, cum electi sint de praesenti saeculo, & alleati ad sanctorum κλῆρον in caelis.
units.tr: Faith likewise does not cling to earthly things, but flies up on wings to heaven, to the throne of divine majesty. Faithful people are eagles, not jackdaws: the citizenship of the faithful is in heaven, whence they await Christ the Saviour. They seek what is above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God. There they know their treasure to be, since they have been chosen out of the present age and allotted to the lot [κλῆρον] of the saints in heaven.

units.la: Quare & crucem eo ferunt mitius, cum praemoniti sint a Christo, in mundo praefuram ipsos habituros, iuxta Domini Prophetiam: Quicunq; discipulus meus esse vult, renunciet sibi ipsi & tollens crucem suam, sequatur me. Hoc non alio modo fieri possit ad gloriam, exemplo Dn. Salvatoris, cuius ducuntur promissione: O ὁ πιστεύων ... Mundi crucem atra esse pernorunt, h.e. maledictam, & vestibulum aeternorum cruciatuum, sed autem corripi a Domino, ne cum mundo damnentur: Sanctificata enim crux fidelium in cruce Christi, sub cuius ipsi aspiciis hic maerent & merent.
units.tr: Therefore they also bear the cross more gently, since Christ has forewarned them that they will have tribulation in the world, according to the Lord's prophecy: Whoever wishes to be my disciple, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me. This cannot be done in any other way to glory, after the example of our Lord the Saviour, whose promise leads them on: He who believes [ὁ πιστεύων] ... They have learned well that the cross of the world is black, that is, accursed, and the threshold of eternal torments; but to be chastened by the Lord, lest they be condemned with the world. For the cross of the faithful is sanctified in the cross of Christ, beneath whose shadow they mourn and deserve here.

units.la: Lux & Dux fidelium est Verbum. Fides enim Verbum intuetur. Non est fides ubi non est verbum, sed tantum opinio. Unum & solum Verbum sequuntur fideles praeuium: Nihil consultantes cum carne & sanguine, sed rationem & intellectum captiuum ducunt sub obsequium Christi, confirmantes quod verax Deus sit, nihil insitiantes. Et sequuntur, Verbum quidem Euangelii in fide: Verbum legis in vita: Quare confidenter dicunt cum Apostolo: Gloriamur in adflictionibus, scientes quod tribulatio patientiam operatur: Patientia autem probationem: probatio vero spem: Spes autem non confundit, quia charitas Dei diffusa est in cordibus nostris per Sp.S. qui datus est nobis: Et cum regio Psalte: Nisi Verbum tuum consolatio mea fuisset, periissem vtiq; in adflictionibus meis: Concludunt q;: Quis nos separabit, &c. Certi sumus quod neq; mors neq; vita, neq; Angeli, neq; principatus, neq; virtutes, neq; praesentia, neq; futura, neq; altitudo, neq; profunditas separabunt nos a dilectione Dei quae est in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: The light and guide of the faithful is the Word. For faith looks upon the Word. Where there is no Word, there is no faith, but only opinion. The faithful follow one and only Word as their leader: taking no counsel with flesh and blood, but leading reason and understanding captive into obedience to Christ, confirming that God is true, and denying nothing. They follow the Word of the Gospel in faith and the Word of the law in life. Therefore they confidently say with the Apostle: We glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation works patience; and patience, experience; and experience, hope; and hope does not disappoint, because the love of God is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us. And with the royal Psalmist: Unless your word had been my comfort, I would surely have perished in my afflictions. They also conclude: Who shall separate us, etc.? I am certain that neither death nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, shall separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus.
ARCVS NIMIS INTENSVS, facile rumpitur.

units.la: Sacrosanctarum dulcis symphonia legum est, Omnibus & numeris dulcior Harmonicis: Candida si nostris regnet dilectio rebus, Annuet & summi gratia larga Dei.
units.tr: The sweet harmony of the sacred laws is sweeter than any music in every measure; if sincere love reigns in our affairs, the generous grace of the highest God will also give its assent.

units.la: Legum Cynosuram obseruare nemo bonus detrectat, in quocunque ordine: Quicquid extra harum limites vagatur, vis est & violentia non durabilis. Talis est harmonia verbi, legum, iurisq; scripti, vt suauius adficiat quam vlla Symphonia vocum vel chordarum. Vicissim vt si nimis intendatur fides, fit vt aut rumpantur, aut ingratissime [illegible, ~3 letters] aures feriat, ita vel prudentia vel violentia extra & praeter leges, verbum, iusq; aut rumpitur, ac sua mole corruit, aut ingrata est diisq; piisq;, inque fine turpissimum post se fætorem relinquit.
units.tr: No good person objects to following the Cynosure of the laws, in whatever order. Whatever wanders beyond their limits is force and violence, which does not last. Such is the harmony of the Word, of the laws and of written right, that it affects the mind more sweetly than any symphony of voices or strings. Conversely, if a string is stretched too tight, it either snaps or grates harshly on the ears. So too, prudence or violence outside and beyond the laws, the Word and right either breaks and collapses under its own weight, or is displeasing to gods and good people, and in the end leaves behind a most foul stench.

units.la: In Ecclesiastico munere si fides nimis intendantur, & acumini ingenii quis nimis fidat, aut efferatur, quanta (Deum immortalem!) dissonantia exsurgit in articulis fidei, vt dato vno inconuenienti & absurdo Theologi o fexcenta sequentur continuo & amplius. Semper periculosum fuit, & scrutari extra verbum. In verbo se suo Deus quaeri vult & inueniendum se promittit. Verbum fasciae sunt, quibus Christus inuoluitur, cui tu est monium omnes ferunt Prophetae. Sequenda analogia, & interpretanda sunt pauca secundum plura, non contra plura. Optimus lector scripturarum & Doctor is est, qui dictorum intelligentiam exspectat ex dictis potius, quam importat, & qui refert magis quam infert, Sententia scripturae quaerenda est in ipsa scriptura. Nulla n. Prophetia est ... Qui vero ex tolerabili verbi luce subuehitur ad intolerabilem & inaccessam lucem in qua Deus habitat, is a gloria maiestatis facile oppressus Icarium in morem ruit, eo altius quo sublatus. Non decet seruum arcana Domini scrutari, nec calorum arcana discutere, sed de caelestibus rebus conuenit honesta & gloriosa sapere. Suffi- ciunt diuinitus inspirata scriptura ad ea quae credenda & facienda sunt. Omnis enim scriptura ... vtilis est ad docendum, ad arguendum, ad corrigendum, ad erudiendum in iustitia, vt perfectus sit homo Dei ad omne opus bonum instructus. Relinquendus Deus est in maiestate, & amplexandus Deus ut ...
units.tr: In ecclesiastical office, if faith is stretched too tight, and if someone trusts too much in the sharpness of his wit or is carried away by it, what a dissonance (immortal God!) arises in the articles of faith, so that once one inappropriate and absurd point is granted, a thousand more follow at once, and more. It has always been dangerous to search beyond the Word. God wishes to be sought in his own Word and promises to be found there. The Word is the swaddling cloth in which Christ is wrapped; to him all the Prophets bear witness. One must follow the analogy, and a few passages must be interpreted according to many, not against many. The best reader and teacher of the Scriptures is the one who looks for the meaning of sayings from the sayings themselves rather than bringing it in from outside, and who draws out more than he puts in. The sense of Scripture is to be sought in Scripture itself. For no prophecy ... But whoever is carried from the tolerable light of the Word up to the intolerable and inaccessible light in which God dwells, he is easily overwhelmed by the glory of majesty and falls like Icarus, the higher he is raised the deeper his fall. It is not fitting for a servant to pry into the secrets of the Lord, nor to investigate the secrets of heaven, but it is proper to think honourably and gloriously about heavenly things. Scripture divinely inspired is sufficient for what is to be believed and done. For all Scripture ... is profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, equipped for every good work. God must be left in his majesty, and God embraced as ...

units.la: In functione Politica, vt maxime quis haud iniuste sententiam rogarit, iniustus tamen est, qui absque lege. Quicquid extra leges fertur, vis & violentia est. Nullum autem violentum diuturnum. Erubescunt sine lege loqui; Erubescant & sine lege effectui quid dare. Leges rogantur, non tam aliu, quam ipsis Nomothetis. Solus Deus ... est, leges fert, nullas patitur: IPSE TAMEN SIBI LEX est. Tyrannorum hoc est: sic VOLO, STAT PRO SENTENTIA VOLUNTAS. Non quod libet, liceat: sed quod licet libeat; sub Deo se esse meminerint magistratus: apud quem non est respectus personarum.
units.tr: In political office, although one might not unjustly ask for a verdict on almost anything, yet the one who acts without law is unjust. Whatever is carried out outside the laws is force and violence. But no violence lasts long. They blush to speak without law; let them also blush to bring anything about without law. Laws are proposed not so much for others as for the lawgivers themselves. God alone ... is, he gives laws, and suffers none: yet he is a law to himself. This belongs to tyrants: thus I will it; my will stands in place of a judgement. What pleases may not be permitted, but what is permitted should please; magistrates should remember that they are under God, with whom there is no respect of persons.

units.la: In omnibus autem actionibus nostris moderetur charitas. Amoris officium est, pascere Dominicum gregem, in utroque statu: militet illud Apostoli: ... γινωσκητω πασιν ανθρωποις, ο κυριος εγγυς.
units.tr: In all our actions charity should moderate. It is the duty of love to feed the Lord's flock, in either condition; let that saying of the Apostle hold good: ... [gignōskete pasin anthrōpois, ho kyrios engys] "Let it be known to all men: the Lord is at hand."
PRVDENTER AGE.

units.la: Lanigeras prudenter oues age pasce, tuumq; Nunquam negligito pastor amice gregem. Quisua nunc pascit sapienter ovilia, quondam Intrabit coeli pastor ovisq; domum.
units.tr: Shepherd, feed the woolly sheep prudently, and never neglect your flock, my friend. He who now feeds the folds wisely will one day enter the home of heaven, the shepherd and his sheep together.

units.la: De Thalete Milesio fertur, quod astris futurorum indagandorum gratia intentus in paludem, quae ante pedes erat ceciderit: quem vetula quaedam conspicata effusè deriserit, arguens stultitiae, quod longe absentium scrutator à praesentibus non potuerit cauere. Talem Thaletem hic vides, qui in longinquum prospiciens, suarum, quae ante pedes sunt, ouium nullam ducit rationem. Quis numerabit omnes ac singulos hodienum huiusmodi Thaletes, qui futurorum curiosi sectatores ac spectatores, eorum, quae imminent ceruicibus, obliquiscuntur. ¶ Videas multos Ecclesiasticos qui rei ita tenaciter haerent familiari, augediíq; studeant opibus, &c, ut domi prospiciat suae, ita laborant, ut nulla prorsus ouium, diuinitus atq; humanitus sibi concreditarum, & pro quibus aliquando coram tribunali Christi grauissimam reddituri sunt rationem, ab ipsis ducatur ratio. Hi sunt Pastores, qui semetipsos pascunt, adipem comedunt, & lanam induunt, quod opinum est, mactant, gregem non pascunt. Morbo affectas non confirmant, aegrotam non curant, confractam non obligant, depulsam non reducunt, pereuntem non requirunt; Sed ut dominantur in eas quorum sanguinem Dominus ab ipsorum manibus reposcet. Talium Deus venter est, quae moritur est, aiunt, vah moriatur! Plutoni sacra faciunt, non Christo. Mercenarij sunt, veniente lupo fugiunt. Mισθωτὸς non serui Christi. Vae illu quoniam Euangelium non praedicant, cuius cum se tum eos, qui audiunt, saluos facere possint. Lupus certe non venit, nisi ut interficiat, hos inclament Molossi oportet, aut proprio tergore luant, propria pelle pendant. O bone Iesu, quantus horum numerus interfacerdotes tuos! Boni Pastores quidem esset tondere pecus non deglubere, quae Tiberii Imp. olim vox erat. Inuenias autem multos Dynastas & Primates, qui depilent suos, exugant suos, excoriant suos, similes illis de quibus Spiritus S. Coegerunt, inquit, Aegyptij filios Israelis seruire per seuitiam. Nō Pastores sunt tales, sed carnifices. Ο ... vt inter Gentiles ... ille dicebat. Occinat omnibus auicula illa Maximiliani Imp. capta prius, post ob magni thesauri demonstrandi promissionem dimissa, suum: TVA SERVA Infonetq; auribus & menti illud nostri Poeta. Fide Deo, tua cautus agas, aliena relinquas, Dissimulas & sunt fi qua ferenda feras. Tela venenata non cures inuida lingua, Tuq; tuam rege, dic pauca, tacenda tace. Sic placidos curret facilis tibi vita per annos Et dabit oranti mollia fata Deus.
units.tr: It is told of Thales of Miletus that, intent on the stars to find out the future, he fell into a pond that lay at his feet. An old woman who saw it laughed at him openly, rebuking him for folly: a man who searched into distant things could not beware of what was present. You see here such a Thales, who, looking far off, takes no account of the sheep that are at his feet. Who will count all and each of the Thaleses of this kind today, eager pursuers and watchers of the future, who forget the things that hang over their necks? ¶ You may see many churchmen who cling so tenaciously to family affairs and strive to increase their wealth that they look after their own household so carefully, yet take no account at all of the sheep committed to them by God and by men, for whom they will one day render a most grave account before the judgement seat of Christ. These are the ministers who feed themselves, eat the fat and clothe themselves with the wool; what is fat they slaughter, they do not feed the flock. They do not strengthen the diseased, they do not heal the sick, they do not bind up the broken, they do not bring back the driven away, they do not seek the lost; but they rule over them with harshness, whose blood the Lord will require at their hands. For such men their belly is their god; when it dies, they say, "Alas, let it die!" They sacrifice to Pluto, not to Christ. They are hirelings, they flee when the wolf comes. [misthōtos] not servants of Christ. Woe to them, since they do not preach the Gospel by which they can save both themselves and those who hear. Surely the wolf comes only to kill; let the mastiffs bark at these men, or let them pay with their own hide, hang with their own skin. O good Jesus, how great is the number of these among your priests! It would indeed be the mark of a good shepherd to shear the flock, not to flay it, as once the saying of the Emperor Tiberius was. But you will find many lords and chiefs who pluck their own people, drain them, and flay them, like those of whom the Holy Spirit says: "They made the sons of Israel serve with cruelty." Such men are not shepherds but butchers. ... as among the Gentiles ... he used to say. Let that little bird of Emperor Maximilian, once captured and afterwards released on the promise of showing a great treasure, sing its song to everyone: TVA SERVA (keep your own). And let that saying of our poet sound in the ears and minds of all: Trust God, act with caution, leave what is another's alone; overlook what can be overlooked, and bear what must be borne. Let not an envious tongue heed poisoned arrows; rule your own tongue, say little, and keep silent what must be kept silent. So will an easy life run smoothly for you through peaceful years, and God will give gentle fates to the one who prays.
The Illusion of Spirits in Glass

units.la: O laudis stimule! ô malè quid mortalia cogis Pectora; vel summum deseruisse Deum! Hoc age, & hoc sape, quod diuino munere gratis Concessum est, ita Iouæq; frueris ope.
units.tr: O goad of praise! Oh, what evil you drive mortal hearts to, even to abandon God Most High! Do this, and keep doing it, what has been granted freely by divine gift, and so you enjoy the help of Jove.

units.la: Fatuitate, curiositate, temeritate, atq; adeo impietate præsens hoc nostrum seculum nihil concedit, nihil, inquam, concedit prisci Gentilium temporibus, siquidem æqua rem lance librare lubeat. Miramur fatuitatem Cascorum, qui in montibus, collibus, conuallibus saltantes videre Faunos, Satyros, & alios id genus Deos commentitios potuerint, atq; adeo illis cohabitare, colludere, familiarissime conuiuere, miremur potius atq; iterum miremur, quos hodie experimur Christianos, viuos, sanos, scientes, volentes, viuis cohabitare dæmonibus, diabolis, Satanæ emissitiis. Detestatur Apostolus Gentium μωεἰων, qui mutauerunt gloriam incorruptibilis Dei in similitudinem imaginis corruptibilis hominis & volucrum & quadrupedum & serpentium, multo magis nos detestemur Moriamne dicam an impietatem multorum hodie, qui viuos in vitris alunt diabolos, quorum operas & consilia exquirunt, quibusque viuis suauiter cohabitant, conuiuunt, colludunt, & quibufcum omne initium suorum laborum faciunt atq; finem. Non iam dico Lamias, omitto striges, taceo stultum veneficarum vulgus & agmen † Menippæum, de iis loquor, qui in consilium adhibent diabolos, Theologi, Theologastri, Iureconsulti, Medici, Medicastri, Philosophi, Philosophastri, Chymici, & reliquus Doctorum, literatorumque manipulus, qui donis suis diuinitus concessis non contenti ad diaboli auxilia confugiunt, & Beelzebulis opem exposcunt. Hoccine illud est, ô bon!quod Apostolus ait: Quæ communio Christi cum Belial? An non Deus est in Israele, quod consultum itis Beelzebulem? An docuit vos hoc Apostolus, qui dixit: Quicunq; ergo perfecti sumus, hoc sentiamus: & si quid aliter sapitis, & hoc vobis Deus revelabit? Fatuitatem! ô temeritatem! ô impietatem impietatum impiissimam! & proprie rebellionem aduersum Dominum exercituum! Ecquid dicit Figmentum Fictori suo: Qui me sic fecisti, ô Fictores & Factores vestri ipsorum mei! Anne sperare potestis, à patre mendacij proficisci veritatem posse? Proh scelus! Nunquid Euangelista dixit: Vnctio, quam accepistis ab eo, manet in vobis, & non necesse habetis vt aliquis doceat vos: sed sicut vnctio docet vos de omnibus, ita verum est, & non est mendacium; quis vos (malu!) malus dementauit genius? Qui non est mecum, contra me est: & qui non colligit mecum, dispergit. Maneat quisq; in ea vocatione, in qua vocatus est. Qui placide sortem ferre scir;ille sapit. Vt autem muscarum mortuarum vna efficit, vt fœtorem eructet vnguentum pigmentarij, similiter pretiosum nomine Sapientia & gloria virum, fœtidum efficit stoliditatis parum. Et fallere fallique adhuc potestis? Ante abitum fi quis fors talia numina trudat à poena immunem talem fore & absque reatu? ô stoliditatem! imo & diabolicas nugas vestras sub pallio fundamenti venum expenere, vendi-tareque potestis..
units.tr: In foolishness, curiosity, rashness, and indeed impiety, this present age of ours yields to no one. It yields to no one, I say, the times of the ancient Gentiles, if we are willing to weigh the matter on a fair balance. We marvel at the folly of the simpletons who, leaping about on mountains, hills and valleys, could see Fauns, Satyrs and other gods of that kind that they had invented, and could even dwell with them, play with them, and feast with them on the most familiar terms. Yet we ought rather to marvel, and marvel again, at the Christians we see today, who, alive, sound, knowing and willing, live together with demons, devils and Satan's emissaries. The Apostle detests the Gentiles [μωεἰων], "who changed the glory of the incorruptible God into an image made like corruptible man, and to birds, and four-footed beasts, and creeping things" [Rom. 1]. Much more should we detest, shall I call it folly or impiety, the conduct of many today, who keep living devils in glass vessels, whose works and counsels they seek, with whom they live pleasantly, feast, and play, and with whom they make the beginning and end of all their labours. I say nothing now of Lamias, I pass over witches, I keep silent about the foolish crowd of sorceresses and the Menippean troop [†]. I speak of those who take devils into their counsel: theologians, pseudo-theologians, jurists, physicians, quack physicians, philosophers, pseudo-philosophers, chemists, and the rest of the band of learned men and men of letters, who, not content with the gifts divinely granted to them, flee to the aid of the devil and beg the help of Beelzebub. Is this the thing, good heavens, that the Apostle means: "What communion has Christ with Belial?" [2 Cor. 6]. "Is there not a God in Israel, that you go to consult Beelzebub?" [2 Kings 1]. Did the Apostle teach you this, who said: "Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, be thus minded; and if in anything you be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this to you" [Phil. 3]? Folly! Oh rashness! Oh impiety, the most impious of impieties, and properly rebellion against the Lord of hosts! "Does the thing formed say to him who formed it: Why have you made me thus?" [Isa. 29; Rom. 9]. O makers and fashioners of yourselves, can you hope that truth can proceed from the father of lies [John 8]? What a crime! Did not the Evangelist say: "The anointing which you have received from him abides in you, and you need not that any man teach you; but as the same anointing teaches you of all things, so it is true, and is no lie" [1 John 2]? Who, alas, has driven you mad, some evil genius? "He who is not with me is against me; and he who does not gather with me scatters" [Matt. 12]. Let each one remain in the calling in which he was called [1 Cor. 7]. He who knows how to bear his lot calmly is wise. "As dead flies make the ointment of the perfumer give off a stench, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honour" [Eccl. 10]. And can you still deceive and be deceived? If anyone perhaps, before departing this life, thrusts such divinities upon you, does he think he will be free of punishment and without guilt? Oh stupidity! Indeed you can even sell and offer for sale your diabolical trifles under the cloak of a foundation, and so pass them off for money.

units.la: ARBOR MALOS MALA FERT, fructus, bona sed bonos.
units.tr: A bad tree bears bad fruit; good things bear good fruit, but good people.

units.la: [Woodcut emblem: a tree bearing banners inscribed Vis, Luxuria, Philarguria, Philutimia, Curiositas, Superbia, Invidia, and a banner reading "Dic quibus in terris, nec eris mihi parvus Apollo"; figures of clergy seated beneath the tree, a skeleton and a devil in the branches.] Dic quibus in terris, & eris mihi magnus Apollo, Tota Sacerdotum crimine turba vacet? Est etiam in sanctis labes, nec dicere quicquam Est pura à naevis mens mea tota, potest.
units.tr: [Woodcut emblem: a tree bearing banners inscribed Vis, Luxuria, Philarguria, Philutimia, Curiositas, Superbia, Invidia, and a banner reading "Tell me in what lands, and you shall be to me a great Apollo, does the whole crowd of priests stand free of guilt?"; figures of clergy seated beneath the tree, a skeleton and a devil in the branches.] Tell me in what lands, and you shall be to me a great Apollo, whether the whole throng of priests is free from fault. There is a stain even in the saints, and my mind, wholly pure from blemishes, cannot say anything.

units.la: Quaesitum est: An propter vitia personarum, merito patiantur officia ipsa vocationum? Praesens noster ἐπιλημμα respondet & concludit negatiue, aut dubie.Siquidem radix sancta sit, ait Apostolus, surculos necessario sanctos fore. Si qui vero surculi sint minus boni, non esse eos de radice, sed aliunde insitos degenerēs, ἀκάρπως: Omnis alias arbor bona fert bonos fructus, & arbor omnis mala, malos fructus. Fac arborem bonam & bonos ferét, fac malam & malos ferēt fructus. Arbor mala bonos non ferre fructus, nec bona malos, potest: Ita ex bonis Dei donis, ordinibus, sanctionibusque per se non nisi bona prouenire & laudabilia possunt, & si quid secus fuerit deprehensum exploratumque, non ipsis officiis id sed personarum vitiis acceptum ferri debet. Omnis plantatio ait Dn.Saluator, quam non plantauit per meum coelestis, eradicabitur. Vel, si mitius interpretari malimus: Si cuius opus arserit, detrimentum patietur: Ipse autem saluus erit, sic tamen quasi per ignem. Sane, in multis labimur omnes: & quis est qui faciat bonum, qui non peccet? iustus septies de die cadit, & resurgit. Imo omnium renatorum iustitia tam iusta ac pura est, quam pannus est menstruata. An enim non curiosus Dauid, scire discupiens numerum feminis Israelitici; Petrus nunquid curiosus; quando dicenti: Domine, hic autem quid? Dominus, si ait: cum volo manere donec veniam, quid ad te? Non omnes sancti intonant cum Dauide: Domine non est exaltatum cor meum: Multis etiam datur stimulus carnis, vt ne se extollant nimis: Nunquid & inuidus Iosua, glisecentis gloriae Eldadi & Medaedi aemulus, cui, Domine mi Mosche, cohibe eos, aienti, respondet Moyses: An invides tu mea causa? vtinam totus populus Iehoua essent Prophetae, indente Iehoua Spiritum suum illis. De inuidia Eliabi dicere quid attinet? Philotimia nunquid & Apostolos Domini inuasit & peruasit lues, altercantes inter se de Primatu; Decantatur Luxuria Dauidis: & vis violentiaq; contra Vriam Hetthęu Misargyria Danielis etiam apud bonos saepe rara est: & vel in intimis sodalitii Christi recessibus latet furac Satanas, cui vel ipse Dominus τῶν χειρῶν ἕνεκα venalis fit. Quae cum ita sint, dic quibus in terris (nec erit mihi paruus Apollo) fit, qui non in aliquo impingat? Beatus qui minimis vrgetur. Si qua autem ex radice vere, proprie, tantum protruduntur idola, desertio veri Dei, idololatria, rebellio erga superiores. Gigantomachia, caedes Regum, Principum, caedes, latrocinia, stupra, incestus, adulteria, Sodomiae, furta, rapinae, obtrectationes & similia vel maiora, si quae possunt esse aut dici scelerum βδελυγμάτων, ea radix vere ac proprie mala esse ac dici potest, debetque.
units.tr: The question is: whether the offices of callings themselves rightly suffer on account of the faults of the persons who hold them. Our present assumption [ἐπίλημμα] answers and concludes in the negative, or at least doubtfully. For, the Apostle says, if the root is holy, the shoots must necessarily be holy. If any shoots are less good, they are not from the root but grafted in from elsewhere, and they are degenerate and unfruitfully [ἀκάρπως]: every good tree bears good fruit, and every bad tree bad fruit. Make the tree good and it will bear good fruit; make it bad and it will bear bad fruit. A bad tree cannot bear good fruit, nor a good tree bad. So from God's good gifts, orders and ordinances, nothing but good and praiseworthy things can arise in themselves; and if anything otherwise is detected and proved, it must be charged not to the offices themselves but to the faults of the persons. Every plant, says the Lord Saviour, which my heavenly Father has not planted, will be uprooted. Or, if we prefer a gentler interpretation: If anyone's work is burned, he will suffer loss; but he himself will be saved, yet as through fire. Indeed, we all stumble in many things: and who is there who does good and does not sin? A righteous man falls seven times a day and rises again. Indeed, the righteousness of all the reborn is as filthy as a menstruous cloth. Was not David curious, desiring to know the number of the women of Israel? Was not Peter curious, when, on being told, Lord, but what of this man? the Lord said: If I will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Not all the saints sing with David: Lord, my heart is not lifted up. To many too a goad is given for the flesh, lest they exalt themselves too much. Was not Joshua envious, a rival of the rising glory of Eldad and Medad, to whom, when he said, My lord Moses, restrain them, Moses replied: Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the people of the LORD were prophets, and that the LORD would put his Spirit upon them. Why speak of the envy of Eliab? Did not the plague of ambition [Philotimia] also invade and overrun the Apostles of the Lord, when they quarrelled among themselves about primacy? David's lust is famously sung; and violence and force against Uriah the Hittite; the avarice of Daniel is even among good men often rare; and even in the inmost recesses of Christ's fellowship the thieving Satan lies hidden, by whom even the Lord himself was made venal for the sake of the hands [τῶν χειρῶν ἕνεκα]. Since these things are so, tell me in what lands (you will not be a little Apollo to me) is there anyone who does not stumble in something? Blessed is he who is pressed by the smallest things. But if, from a root, truly, properly, only idols sprout forth, desertion of the true God, idolatry, rebellion against superiors, the slaughter of kings and princes, murders, robberies, rapes, incest, adulteries, sodomies, thefts, plunderings, slander and similar things, or greater ones, if any can be or be called among the abominations [βδελυγμάτων] of crimes, then that root can and must truly and properly be called evil.
LET THE OTHER PART ALSO BE HEARD.

units.la: Si censura virum damnet nil tale merentem,
units.tr: If censure condemns a man who deserves nothing of the kind,
and acquits the guilty, it bears no light crime.
Therefore the judge should not finish the case after hearing one side,
but must pronounce judgment after hearing both men.

units.la: Occursare caue, ferit hoc emblema bicorne, altero Ecclesiasticos, altero seculares cornu. Sunt quos non contentos verbo diuino conscendere cælū & penetralia cælestium aditorū scrutari iuuat. Magna hæc & blasphema temeritas est, maiestatis diuinę gloria reprimenda, opprimenda, comprimenda. Non est scala, qua in cælū scanditur, nisi illa Iacobæa, hieroglyphica Christi, dicentis: Ego sum via, veritas, & vita, erigitur illa in verbo Euangelio, inq; ipsum cælum cælorum porrigitur. Prope autem est verbum istud, in ore tuo & in corde tuo est, nec est quod dicas; Quis est, qui ascendet in calum? id est Christum deducere. Aut quis descendet in abyssum? id est Christum à mortuis reuocare. Quid n. est quod reliquum sit & obscurum? In verbo Dei plena sunt omnia & perfecta, vt à pleno & perfecto. Absit ergo vt obloquatur homo diuinis & à Deo inspiratis scripturis, quasi non omnia inter se consonent. Quare non asseramus slateras dolosas, vbi appendamus quod volumus, & quomodo volumus, pro arbitrio nostro, dicentes: hoc graue, hoc leue est, sed asseramus diuinam slateram de scripturis sanctis tanquam depræcpiu Domini is, & in illa quid sit grauius appendamus, imo non appendamus, sed à Domino appensa recognoscamus.
units.tr: Beware of running against: this two-horned emblem strikes at the ecclesiastical horn and the secular horn. There are those who, not content with the divine word, delight to climb to heaven and to search the inner chambers of the heavenly courts. This is a great and blasphemous rashness, to be restrained, crushed and suppressed by the glory of the divine majesty. The ladder by which one climbs to heaven is not any other than that Jacob's ladder, the hieroglyph of Christ, who says: I am the way, the truth, and the life; it is raised up in the word of the Gospel and stretches out to the very heaven of heavens. But the word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart, and there is no need to say: Who will ascend into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down; or who will descend into the abyss? that is, to call Christ back from the dead. For what is left that is hidden and obscure? In the word of God all things are full and perfect, as from what is full and perfect. Far be it, therefore, that a man should speak against the divine Scriptures inspired by God, as if they did not agree among themselves. Let us not therefore hold up deceitful scales, where we weigh what we wish, and as we wish, according to our own judgment, saying: this is heavy, this is light; but let us hold up the divine scale of the holy Scriptures, as the command of the Lord, and in it let us weigh what is heavier; or rather, let us not weigh it ourselves, but recognise what has been weighed by the Lord.

units.la: Sunt qui Iudicia de rebus sacris, & ad fidem bene formandam, vitamque pie transigendam pertinentibus anticipant, & ex præconceptis opinionibus idola sibi statuminant, alterutrius alicuius partis clamoribus, interpestiuisq; cõdemnationibus præoccupati, his vtramq; opplet aurem Satanas, & neutram alteri parti intemeratam relinquit: iniurii illi sunt in Deũ, Deiq; verbum, propriasq; animas, non aduertentes ad Apostoli um monitum: πάντα δοκιμάζετε nec auscultantes illi Christi: scrutamini scripturas Et quæ sunt alia: Ad legem & ad testimonium, &c. Probate Spiritus, &c. Vim alias patitur veritas & fit scriptura ἀνθρώπων, quod fieri vetat Petrus. Insusurrandum igitur erat illis hoc August. Sed nunc nec ego Nicanum nec tu debes Ariminense, tanquam præiudicaturus, proferre, nec ego huius, nec tu illius detinere. Scripturarum authoritatibus non quorumcunq; proprias sed vtriusq; communibus, testib. rep cum re, causa cuiusq; causa, ratio cum ratione certet. Auferantur de medio chartæ nostra, procedat in medium codex Dei. Audi Christum dicentem, audi veritatem loquentem.
units.tr: There are those who anticipate judgments about sacred matters, and about things pertaining to forming the faith well and passing life piously, and set up idols for themselves from preconceived opinions, preoccupied with the outcries and hasty condemnations of one or other party. Satan fills both their ears with these, and leaves neither party untouched for the other. They are unjust towards God and the word of God, and towards their own souls, not heeding the Apostle's warning: Prove all things [πάντα δοκιμάζετε], nor listening to Christ: Search the Scriptures, and the other words: To the law and to the testimony, etc. Test the spirits, etc. Otherwise truth suffers violence and Scripture becomes of men [ἀνθρώπων], which Peter forbids. Therefore it ought to be whispered to them what Augustine said. But now neither I should bring forward the Nicene council, nor you the council of Rimini, as if to pronounce judgment, nor should I hold to this one, nor you to that one. Let not each one's own writings, but the common testimonies of both, be set against the authority of the Scriptures; let thing contend with thing, cause with cause, reason with reason. Let our papers be removed from the middle; let the codex of God come forward into the middle. Hear Christ speaking, hear the truth speaking.

units.la: Deniq; tanguntur etiam Politici, qui sententias præcipitant, non auditis vtrinque sufficienter partibus. Magna in tali præcipitantia malorum lerna est, concurruntque Iniustitia. Stoliditas. Profopolepsia. Confusio, vt non incongrue dixerit, quicunq; dixerit:
units.tr: Finally, politicians are also touched upon, who hastily pronounce sentences without hearing both parties sufficiently. In such hasty judgment there is a great hydra of evils, and there come together injustice, stupidity, partiality, confusion, as whoever said it aptly put it:

units.la: Adpœnitendum properat, cito qui iudicat. Militat hic quoq; tritum illud: Audiatur altera pars. Nota est, Alexandri Magni Regis mos, comprimentis ad accusationem Actoris dextram aurem vt illibatam eam Reo sese defensuro conferuet, nec carent exemplis quoque in vtramque partem sacræ literæ.
units.tr: He who judges hastily hurries to repent. This also fits the well-worn saying: Let the other side be heard. The custom of Alexander the Great, the king, is well known, who pressed his right ear shut while the accuser spoke, so that he might keep it unharmed to hear the accused who was about to defend himself; and the sacred letters also have examples on both sides.
The Trojans sin within the walls and without them.
The giants that scale heaven rule the lawless ages,
And no one bears his powers within his station.
So hasten our return, good Christ, our Redeemer;
Be present, and set a limit to evils for ever.

units.la: Fabulati sunt Poetæ de Gigantomachia quadam, qua Gigantes quia in ferrea mundi ætate contra Iouem conspirarint, & congestis montibus coelum oppugnare contenderint, cui fabulæ extructio turris Babylonica forsan occasionem dedit. Sed meliorum iudicio nunc grassatur ferreum illud seculum, infaniuntq; Gigantes per omnes Hierarchias, contra quas h.e. contra Aeon Iouem sed Iouam conspirasse videntur בת־שבע & peruersissimi quiq;.
units.tr: The poets tell a fable of a certain Gigantomachia, in which the Giants, because they conspired against Jove in the iron age of the world, and tried to storm heaven by piling up mountains, gave the fable perhaps its occasion in the building of the Babylonian tower. But by the judgement of better men, that iron age now rages, and the Giants run mad through all the hierarchies, conspiring against the Aeon, that is, against Jove, but Jehovah (the Hebrew reads "daughter of seven" [בת־שבע]), and against every most perverse man.

units.la: Exstruunt pii Sacerdotes Domini, templum dominicum voce ac scriptis, tradunt salutarem doctrinam veritatis in thesi, & errores falsaq; dogmata in antithesi confutant, increpant securos, solantur pauidos, docent rudes, exhortantur remissos, verbumq; adeo veritatis recte secant, sed contra hos nituntur Gigantes, qui non tantum non frunt doctrinam salutarem, ad sua desideria coaceruantes sibi magistros, prurientes auribus, auertentes auditum a veritate ad fabulas, sed etiam seruos Dn. perseququntur, pro ludibrio habentes, omnibus modis infestantes, nec ora manusve abstinentes, mendaciis & calumniis circumscribentes, dum vel sedibus expellant, vel interficiant, mensuram veterum prophetiarum, horumq; peccatorum implentes. Saulis, Ierobeami, Manassæ, & alior socii.
units.tr: The pious priests of the Lord build up the Lord's temple by voice and by writing. They deliver the saving doctrine of truth in thesis, and refute errors and false dogmas in antithesis; they rebuke the careless, comfort the fearful, teach the ignorant, exhort the slack, and rightly divide the word of truth. But against these the Giants strive, who not only do not enjoy the saving doctrine, heaping up for themselves teachers to suit their desires, itching in the ears, and turning away their hearing from the truth to fables, but also persecute the servants of the Lord, treating them as a mockery, attacking them in every way, sparing neither mouth nor hands, and beating them down with lies and calumnies, until they either drive them from their seats or kill them, filling up the measure of the old prophecies and of these sins. They are the companions of Saul, Jeroboam, Manasseh, and the others.

units.la: Sub talium Gigantum censum cadunt & Theologastri, vel semper discentes, nec vnquam ad veritatis agnitionem peruenientes: vel agnoscentes quidem veritatem, verù in iniustitia detinentes, quales plurimos procul dubio per vniuersa orbis Christiani climata reperiri liceret: quibus obstant exitiales furiae φιλοπνεῖαι: φιλοδοξίαι: φιλοπμίαι: φιλαχγυγεῖαι: αρεσκιαι, & alia monstra, quo minus veritati victas dent manus. Nunquid hi contra Deum eiusque veritatem confpirasse videntur?
units.tr: Among such Giants fall also the pseudo-theologians, who are always learning and never coming to the knowledge of the truth, or who indeed acknowledge the truth but hold it in unrighteousness. Doubtless many such men could be found throughout every region of the Christian world. Hindering them from yielding their hands conquered to the truth are the deadly furies of vainglory, ambition, avarice, pleasure-seeking, self-pleasing, and other monsters. Do not these men seem to have conspired against God and his truth?

units.la: Inter optimates tales Gigantes sunt plurimi, qui hoc vnice studio habent, vt pios ac doctos ministros premant, & pro mancupis, afinisq; & pedum scabellis suorum vtantur, sacerdotes risus ac lusus ipsis fiunt in conuiuiis dicasteriis, & aliis congressibus, vt Ezechiel de se queritur.
units.tr: Among the nobles there are very many such Giants, who have this one aim: to oppress the pious and learned ministers, and to use them as servants, asses, and footstools for their own purposes; the ministers become a laughingstock and a joke to them at feasts, in courts, and in other gatherings, just as Ezekiel complains of himself.

units.la: Manus rapaces a bonis Ecclesiasticis non abstinent, Harpiis peiores ipsis, interim de V.I.DD. titulo sibi primas vsurpantes, apud quos nihil minus in vsu est, quam illud alterius iuris: semel Deo dicatum non debet amplius transferri ad profanos vsus. Ain' tu, an non optimo iure Gigantibus accenseri huiusmodi putes?
units.tr: Their grasping hands do not keep off the goods of the Church, being worse than the Harpies themselves; meanwhile they claim for themselves the first place under the title of "Your Honours," among whom nothing is less in use than that principle of another's right: what has once been dedicated to God ought not to be transferred again to profane uses. Tell me, do you not think that such men deserve, by the best right, to be counted among the Giants?

units.la: Rebellibus contra potestates orbis Christianus non caret, qui diruunt Curias, Leges, Principatus, faces submittunt, quibus omnes politicæ bonæ sanctiones, totusque S. Magistratus ordo conflagret: in quos non fraga'ium gerit magistratus. Huiusmodi sunt negantes vel detrectantes debita potestatibus omnis generis obsequia, & omnibus bonis constitutionibus cornua obuertentes.
units.tr: The Christian world is not without rebels against the powers, who overthrow courts, laws, and principalities, and set fire to them, by which all the good sanctions of civil life and the whole sacred order of the magistracy are burned up. Against such men the magistrate does not bear the sword in vain. Of this kind are those who deny or refuse the due obedience owed to every sort of authority, and who turn their horns against all good constitutions.

units.la: Denique, cum Hierarchicus et Oeconomiæ status sit, quis non in eo videt gigantes. Immorigeros liberos; inofficiosos seruos; degenerem iuuentutem; patrum bonorum prodigam sobolem; quare si super illos Iuppiter diluuiu aquarum immisit, quis scit an non super hos eluuia ignium & extremi incendii immittere primo quoq; tempore decreuerit?
units.tr: Finally, since there is a hierarchical and domestic order, who does not see Giants in it? Disobedient children; unfaithful servants; a degenerate youth; the prodigal offspring of good fathers. Therefore, if Jupiter sent a flood of waters upon those, who knows whether he has not resolved to send, at the earliest opportunity, deluges of fire and the final conflagration upon these?
GNOMON, OR THE TYPE OF THE CHRISTIAN LIFE.

units.la: [engraving: emblem of a globe with crown and arms, holding a mace and a serpent-entwined cross, a Decalogus tablet and an hourglass below, hands pointing from the sides, and a bird at upper left; described under notes] Vt præsens sine labe queas transmittere seclum, Vtq; homini possis gratus & esse Deo: Ruštantes gemitus simplex imitare columbas, Serpentumq; colas quam sapienter opus.
units.tr: So that you may be able to pass this age without stain, and may be pleasing both to man and to God: imitate the simple doves in their plaintive moaning, and cultivate the serpent's work, which is so wise.

units.la: Omnes homines summa ope niti decet, vt vitam pie ac pacifice hic transigant, quod certe caput est felicitatis nostrae in hac terra,in hoc seculo malo.Quo autem pacto fieri id possit,hoc compendio docet Dn.Saluator in Euangelio;dicens:Ecce ego mitto vos sicut oues in medio luporum : estote ergo prudentes,sicut serpentes,& simplices sicut columba. Columbinam simplicitatem,vna cum serpentina prudentia imitari iubet nobis. Vtrumq; & columbarum ac serpentum genus multarū rerum,in fide&vita vtilium,hieroglyphica sunt.
units.tr: All men ought to strive with all their might to pass their lives here piously and peaceably, which is certainly the chief of our happiness on this earth, in this evil age. How this may be done, our Lord and Saviour teaches in the Gospel in a summary, saying: Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and simple as doves. He bids us imitate the dovelike simplicity together with the serpentine prudence. Both the kind of dove and the kind of serpent are hieroglyphs of many things useful for faith and life.

units.la: Illæ lenitatis, vt est in versu mitis titulus columba. Lenitas fructus est Spiritus eius,qui in specie columbę in baptismo Christi apparet:& est necessaria virtus,vt placide ac pacifice degas:Pacifici filii Dei vocantur:Mites terrā possidebūt.
units.tr: The dove signifies gentleness, as in the verse, the dove is the emblem of meekness; gentleness is the fruit of the Spirit, who appeared in the form of a dove at the baptism of Christ. It is a necessary virtue, so that you may live calmly and peaceably: the children of God are called peacemakers; the meek shall inherit the earth.

units.la: Eædem,linguæ frenandæ,vt dicitur in versu:restro non ladit,virtutem primā effeputa compescere linguam,proximus ille Deo qui scit ratione tacere. Agite, inquit Psaltes diuinus:auscultate mihi, reuerentiam Iehoua doceo vos: quis est ille qui desiderat vitā,amat dies,amat frui bono; custodi linguam tuam à malo, & labia tua ne loquantur fraudem. Næ ille compendiosissimum viuendæ vitæ huius compendium inoeptus est,linguam qui didicit frænare.
units.tr: The same dove signifies the bridling of the tongue, as the verse says: He who does not harm with his tongue; the first virtue is to hold the tongue in check; that man is near to God who knows how to keep silent with reason. Come, says the divine Psalmist, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD. Who is the man who desires life and loves days that he may enjoy good? Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit. Indeed, he has begun the most compendious summary of living this life who has learned to bridle his tongue.

units.la: Gemitus itidem,qui sunt preces sanctorum. Non quærit Deus dilationem in tortura (cras) sed confessionem in gemitu columbino. Hæc regis illius vox est, qui post exantlatum grauissimum agonem dicebat: vt grus aut hirundo ita pipiebam, gemebam vt columba.
units.tr: Likewise the sighing, which are the prayers of the saints. God does not seek delay under torture (tomorrow), but confession in the sigh of the dove. This is the voice of that king who, after enduring the most grievous agony, said: Like a crane or a swallow I chattered; I moaned like a dove.

units.la: Beneficentia, vt est in versu:vnguespossidet innocuos. Facile vitam transigit tranquillam, qui abstinet vngues manusue ab aliorum corporibus, fortunisq;& manus adsuescit laboribus ac beneficentiæ, gratus hic est Deo atq; hominibus;quod Apostoli monitum est: Qui furabatur, iam non furetur:magis autem laboret operando manibus suis, vt habeat vnde tribuat necessitatem patienti.
units.tr: Beneficence, as in the verse: the claws possess the harmless. He lives an easy and tranquil life who keeps his claws and hands off the bodies and goods of others, and accustoms his hands to labour and to doing good. Such a man is pleasing to God and to men, as the Apostle admonished: Let him who stole steal no more; but rather let him labour, working with his hands, so that he may have something to give to him who is in need.

units.la: Studii diuini verbi. Nam purum ac mundum animal est columba:pura grana legit:gaudet aquis:quaerit gregesque tuta petit. Munda nos animalia sumus, ruminemus verbum diuinum, quod legamus purum ab humanis traditionibus, gaudere debemuspuris Israelis fontibus salutis, & congregationem sanctorum studiose ac frequenter visitemus, qui hoc in votis habet, fruitur consolatione felicis ac beati viri, arbori secus decursus aquarum plantatæ similis, quæ fructum suum in tempore fert & folia eius non defluent,sed in omnibus prosperabitur.
units.tr: The study of the divine Word. For the dove is a pure and clean animal: it gathers pure grains, rejoices in waters, and seeks out safe flocks. We are clean animals; let us chew over the divine Word, which we should read as pure from human traditions. We ought to rejoice in the pure fountains of Israel's salvation, and diligently and frequently visit the congregation of the saints. Whoever has this in his prayers enjoys the consolation of the happy and blessed man, like a tree planted by the streams of water, which brings forth its fruit in season; its leaf also shall not wither, and in all that he does he shall prosper.

units.la: Simplicitas absque fuco, & dolo qui loquitur facitq; veritatem cum proximo,huic perpetua in monte Domini habitatio delegatur à Psalte Regiosancto. Vere autem ac solide beatus erit si cum columbina simplicitate,scrpentinam coniungat prudentiam:Non enim fatuis nos virginibus similes esse vult,sed prudentibus adsimilari.Nolite (inquit Apostolus)fratres pueri efficissibus,sed malitia paruuli estote,sensibus autem perfecti, vt exercitatos habeatis sensus ad discretionem boni ac mali. Tanquam sapientibus loquor vobis. Vt sapientes ambulate.
units.tr: Simplicity without guile. The one who speaks and deals truly with his neighbour, without deceit, is granted a perpetual dwelling on the holy hill of the Lord by the royal Psalmist. He will be truly and solidly blessed if he joins serpentine prudence to dovelike simplicity. For he does not wish us to be like the foolish virgins, but to be likened to the prudent. Do not be children in understanding, brethren, but be children in malice; yet in understanding be mature, so that you may have your senses exercised to discern good and evil. I speak to you as to wise men. Walk as wise men.

units.la: Serpens magna prudentia cauet ne quid mali patiatur caput,hoc saluo existete omnia ipsi salva nouit.Qui saluus esse vult,ante omnia curet caput salutis FIDEM CATHOLICAM, iustificam, saluifi&m: hac n. iustificamur, stamus, vincimus,& deniq; saluamur,coronā vitæ ac gloriæ reportantes.Perpetim.
units.tr: The serpent, with great prudence, takes care that its head suffers no harm; with the head kept safe, it knows that all its other parts are safe as well. He who wishes to be saved must above all things hold fast to the head of salvation, THE CATHOLIC FAITH, which justifies and saves. For by this we are justified, we stand, we conquer, and at last we are saved, bearing away the crown of life and glory. Perpetually.
EMBLEM: FAITH MADE EFFECTIVE THROUGH LOVE.

units.la: [engraving: allegorical emblem, not transcribed] Si quoties peccant homines sua munera tollat Iova, erit exiguo tempore nulla fides. ALMA Fides, Dilectio, Spes, Prudentia, lustum, Ætherei flatus sunt bona dona Dei.
units.tr: [engraving: allegorical emblem, not transcribed] If Jove were to take away his gifts whenever men sin, there would soon be no faith at all. Nourishing Faith, Love, Hope, Prudence and Justice are the good gifts of God's heavenly breath.

units.la: Indissolubili nexu concatenatæ sunt virtutes in fidelibus atq; electis, ut posita vna (fide scilicet, siquidem vera sit ac viua fides, & non simulacrum potius fidei) ponantur & reliquæ; veræ virtutes sese mutuo ponunt; exhortante Petro: Vos autem (inquit) curam omnem subinferentes ministrate in fide vestra virtutem: in virtute autem scientiam: in scientia autem abstinentiam: in abstinentia autem patientiam: in patientia autem pietatem: in pietate autem amorem fraternitatis: in amore autem fraternitatis: charitatem. Hæc n. vobis cum adsint & superent, non vacuos nec fine fructu vos constituent in Domini nostri Iesu Christi cognitione. Id quod præsens hæc nostra figura liquidum facere conitur. Vides à dextris FIDEM, Dilectionem à Lœua mutuas sibi manus operasq; complicatas, concatenatas, coobstrataq; porrigere, plura in vno coniungi atq; copulari corda, ingentesq; ex se eiaculari versus cœlum flammas, inumbrante & χαρισματων superne instillante columba Spir. S. hierogyphica: Inferne nititur corda Triuultia Prudentia, & omnia aqua lance pensiculante iustitia: Lepida sane VIRTVTVM coniunctarum hypotyposis!
units.tr: The virtues are linked together in a bond that cannot be broken in the faithful and the elect, so that when one is posited (namely faith, provided it is true and living faith and not rather a mere image of faith), the rest are posited too. True virtues set one another in place. Peter exhorts: "But you, bringing in all diligence, supply in your faith virtue; and in virtue knowledge; and in knowledge abstinence; and in abstinence patience; and in patience godliness; and in godliness the love of the brethren; and in love of the brethren charity. For if these things be in you and abound, they make you that you shall be neither barren nor unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ." This is what our present figure strives to make plain. You see on the right FAITH, and on the left LOVE, holding out to each other their mutually joined hands and clasped, linked and interlaced works, many hearts joined and coupled into one, and flames shooting up from them towards heaven, with the dove of the Holy Spirit overshadowing them and pouring down the gifts of grace from above, as a hieroglyph. Below, Prudence with her threefold eye rests upon the hearts, and Justice weighs everything in an even balance. A pleasing picture indeed of the virtues joined together!

units.la: Fides, vt id iterato ac sæpiuscule dicamus, certam ex se gignit sobolem, nutritque charitatem, adeo vt sine dilectione fides iactata, fidei tantum sit fucus ac cerussa. Geminum hoc mandatum & donum habemus à Christo, vt qui in ipsum credit, diligat idem & fratres.
units.tr: Faith, to say it again and again, begets a sure offspring and nourishes love, so that faith without love is a mere boast, and is only the paint and whitewash of faith. We have this twofold command and gift from Christ: that whoever believes in him should also love his brothers.

units.la: Fide per dilectionem ἑνότητα vniuntur in vnum complurima corda, vt vnum corpus & vna massa fiant in Domino Iesu, quemadmodum ex multis palmitibus ex vna radice constituitur vitis, & ex multis membris vnum stat uminatur corpus: ita vt vnus panis, vnum corpus sumus multi. Vnde exhortatio Apostolica extructa est: Esfote solliciti seruare VNITATEM Spiritus in vinculo pacis. Vnum corpus & vnus Spiritus, sicut & vocati estis in vna spe vocationis vestræ. Vnus Dominus, vna fides, vnum baptisma, vnus Deus & pater omnium. Quæ sæpenumero repetuntur ἀγνοῖας Domini discipulis.
units.tr: Through faith and love very many hearts are united into one [henotēta], so that in the Lord Jesus they become one body and one mass, just as from many branches growing from one root a vine is made, and from many members one body stands and is made up: so that we, being many, are one bread, one body. Hence the apostolic exhortation: "Be eager to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. There is one body and one Spirit, just as you were called in one hope of your calling. One Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all." These words are repeated very often to the disciples of the Lord [agnoias].

units.la: Fides cum & per dilectionem operatur emittitq; incendium precum, & fauillæ inde vna fide, & vnanimi motu eiaculatæ efficacissimæ sunt apud Deum, ipso Dn. nostro Iesu Christo teste: Ἐὰν δύο ἐξ ὑμῶν συμφωνήσωσιν ... ἐὰν δύο συμφωνήσωσιν περὶ παντὸς πράγματος. Impossibile autem est, vt Hieronymus inquit, multorum preces non exaudiri.
units.tr: When faith works also through love, it sends forth a fire of prayers, and the sparks thrown up from it by one faith and one united movement are most effective with God, our Lord Jesus Christ himself being witness: "If two of you shall agree ... if two shall agree on anything [ean dyo ex hymōn symphōnēsōsin ... ean dyo symphōnēsōsin peri pantos pragmatos]." But it is impossible, as Jerome says, that the prayers of many should not be heard.

units.la: Inumbrans Spiritus S. figurat ortum virtutum fidelium in cordibus, qui non est aliunde, nisi à Spiritu Dei sancto, Spiritu inde gratia & precum dicto: Quid enim oremus sicut oportet, nescimus, verum ipse Spiritus postulat pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus.
units.tr: The overshadowing Holy Spirit signifies the origin of the virtues of the faithful in their hearts, which comes from nothing else but the Holy Spirit of God. From this Spirit comes grace and the saying of prayers: "For we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings that cannot be uttered."

units.la: Deniq; fides parit prudentiam, circumspectionem, σπουδήν: & iustitiam suum cuique tribuentem, τῆς ἰσότητος consultricem, iuxta dominicum monitum: Quacunque vultis vt faciant vobis homines, eadem & vos facite illis. Hæc est caput & summa ἐντολῆς ἀληθείας τῆς πίστεως ἐνεργούμενης.
units.tr: Finally, faith brings forth prudence, circumspection and zeal [spoudēn], and justice giving to each his due, the counsellor of equality [tēs isotētos], according to the Lord's admonition: "Whatever you want men to do to you, do the same to them." This is the head and sum of the commandment of the truth of faith, working through love [ta entolēs alētheias tēs pisteōs energoumenēs].
AT LAST THE GOOD CAUSE TRIUMPHS.

units.la: Altius ecce Aquila hæc auibus volat omnibus, istum Subuolat alma fides sydera ad usq; modum. Nec secus Æstræum librat se ad inania iustum, Exsuperant pariter iustitia atq; fides.
units.tr: Behold, this eagle flies higher than all birds; nourishing Faith rises above them to the stars. Likewise the just man poises himself on the Aethereal heights above emptiness; Justice and Faith together rise above all.

units.la: Scripturae diuinitus inspiratae meminerunt saepenumero Aquilarum, & multarum hieroglyphica rerum sanctarum & utilium faciunt. Paucarum libabimus, inprimis
units.tr: The Scriptures, inspired by God, often mention eagles, and make hieroglyphs of many holy and useful things. Let us touch on a few, first of all:

units.la: FIDELIVM. Aquila Deo chara est: Φιλόφυλος actiue & passiue, sunt fideles: quoniam absq; fide Deo placere haut possibile est.
